CoachHelm read

Lane 2 · CoachHelm read · v6 · Nov 7

CoachHelm read

The read is the board card, opened. Every button, row, bar and chart below is the app’s own markup running on the app’s own CSS, so what you tap here is what ships. Coach and player each get their own version, on a phone and on a desktop.

Try itCoach and playerEvery stateComponent mapMotionDataBuild notes
Real Clubhouse partsButton, Segmented, the deep dive’s rows, the board’s bars, Toast, Menu, Notice and the empty states. The only new CSS is one small layout file.
Actions firstAssign, Dismiss and Message sit right under the read. Today they sit at the bottom of a seven-card stack.
Two viewers, two readsThe coach sees the team pool, likely causes and how sure. The player reads it in second person, against Tour only, and sees only what was counted in their own shots.
Phone and desktop each fitPhone: one pushed screen with three tabs. Desktop: the deep dive with this read selected, every section open, J and K to step.
Motion by the bookPush on the smooth spring, the pill and swaps on settle, a 180ms fade under Reduce Motion. No count-ups, no staggers, nothing moves on first paint.
Numbers that agreeEach read matches the board and the deep dive for the same player. The preview fixture that paired a putting title with approach evidence is fixed here.

Motion

Every move, on the app’s own tokens

From lib/motion.ts. Springs are built as linear() curves from the closed form (ω = 2π ÷ (1.2 × duration), ζ = 1 − bounce), 462ms long. Under Reduce Motion each one becomes a 180ms fade (CH_FADE_MS). With animations off, nothing moves.

MomentWhat movesTokenReduce Motion
Board to read (phone)The read slides in from the right. The board slides 24% left and dims.CH_SPRINGS.smooth 0.26, bounce 0Crossfade
Back (phone)The reverse. The edge swipe follows the finger and lets go on the same spring. Past 35%, or a quick flick, it goes back.smooth, time scaled by distance leftCrossfade
Read to read (desktop)The rail, header and chrome stay still. The main column swaps: the old one fades out, the new one rises 6px.quick 180 out, settle inFade
Tab or window switchThe pill slides to the new tab. The panel swaps as above.settle 0.26, bounce 0.1Pill jumps, panel fades
Trend windowThe line glides from the old shape to the new one. The caption swaps at once.smoothFade
PressThe button dips to 97% and back.press 110None
AssignThe spinner holds the button’s size. The row swaps on settle, then the toast rises.Toast: base 260, CH_EASEFade
How sureThe panel rises in. The chevron turns.settle, smoothFade
More menuGrows from 96% at its corner.base in, quick outFade
NeverNumbers counting up, bars growing into view, staggered lists, anything moving on first paint, a ring filling.

Preview fixture to fix before building (preview/fixtures-coachhelm-read.ts): the approach read is built from slope(…'in-approach') under a putting title, every read reuses the same approach “checked” lines, and every read reuses LADDER(49, 52). The data on this page is the corrected set: one player per read, and numbers that match the board and the deep dive.

Build notes

For the Mac session

  1. In screens/coachhelm/read/ReadPage.tsx, replace the seven cards in cards.tsx with the parts in the map. Most already exist in views/DeepDive.tsx and parts.tsx, so this is mostly moving them.
  2. Phone: mount the read as a pushed screen with PhoneBar, back to CoachHelm and the player’s name as the title for a coach. Put the actions straight under What, Why, Next, When, then a three-tab Segmented.
  3. Desktop: render the deep dive with this read selected and every section open. Add the position and J, K steps to the header aside.
  4. Split by viewer in one place: drop the team pool, the likely arms and the rung for a player. Keep the whole ChReadDetail for a coach.
  5. Delete the read’s own invented classes and its motion: the bars growing in, the 900ms ring and the staggers.
  6. Replace styles/coachhelm-read.css with the file below: its 1,324 lines of .ch-hr- rules on main become about 140. The read is built from Clubhouse’s own parts: the green feature card for its head (as on Home and the live read), the Surface from ui/Surface.tsx for every section, an Inset for evidence. It uses tokens only, plus the live read’s two stance chip colours.
  7. Check on the phone, both themes, Text Size large: tabs keep one line, actions wrap primary first, nothing scrolls sideways.
